From: Cameron Li <security@brightleaf.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:22 -0700
Subject: Vendr profile visibility + temp credential TTL question

Hi Priyom,

Quick one as we prep for the SOC 2 evidence package — Vendr shows our profile as "Visible to all vendors" by default. For the audit window we need two things clarified:

1) Can Redwood set our Vendr profile visibility to a restricted view (Brightleaf + Redwood org) while preserving the portal link for Redwood requested reviewers?
2) Our security team is asking whether Redwood can support extending the temporary upload credential TTL that Vendr issues for S3 proofs from the default 30 days to 90 days for the SOC 2 collection period.

We want to avoid repetitive upload churn for engineers and reduce risk of missing artifacts during the on-site audit. If you need a formal exception request we can sign whatever governance doc you require.

Attached: brightleaf-evidence-sample-policy.pdf (policy excerpt showing retention needs).

Thanks — appreciate the quick read.

Cameron
Cameron Li
Security Lead, Brightleaf
security@brightleaf.com


From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Cameron Li <security@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:03:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr profile visibility + temp credential TTL question

Hi Cameron — thanks for the context and the sample policy.

Looping Kim and Jonas from Security/Portal Ops to confirm:
- Can Vendr profile visibility be scoped to a "Restricted" view (Brightleaf + Redwood reviewer access) rather than public?
- Is there any platform-level constraint (Redwood-side) that prevents allowing Vendr to set the TTL for temporary upload credentials to 90 days for a named account during an audit window?

Kim — if we can support this, we'll need:
- An internal exception record (Confluence) with justification and approval (Brightleaf SOC2 evidence campaign)
- DocuSign-signed exception from Brightleaf accepting responsibility (I can send a template)
- A short expiry/rollback policy (30/60/90 day window + automatic revert) — ops prefers not to leave exceptions open indefinitely.

Cameron — if you're able to sign a quick exception, send the signer name and I'll push this through the exceptions process.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Manager, Vendor Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Priyom / Jonas — okay to approve given the SOC 2 context with the following controls in place:

1) Visibility: Set Vendr profile visibility to "Restricted: Brightleaf + Redwood reviewers" for the audit window (start 2027-08-20, end 2027-11-20). Portal Ops will confirm reviewer list and audit IP allowlist.

2) Temp credential TTL: Approve a 90-day TTL for temporary upload credentials issued to Brightleaf for the stated window only. All credentials will be signed and recorded in the exception Confluence page.

3) Rollback & automation: Portal Ops (Jonas) to schedule a rollback job to restore defaults on 2027-11-21. If a closure request arrives earlier, Marissa will triage.

4) Evidence custody: Brightleaf must acknowledge responsibility for long-lived artifacts in writing (DocuSign). We will not keep an exception without an external sign-off.

Attached: vendr-tempcred-ttl-request.xlsx (proposed dates and reasoning). I can prepare the exception PDF template (redwood-vendr-visibility-exception.pdf) and route for signature.

Kimberly Park
Security Operations Lead

- Rollback: Portal Ops will revert settings on 2027-11-21 automatically unless we receive a closure request.
